Thanks — I’ll create a 12-week general strength program suitable for a 42‑year‑old male desk worker who is 8 months post L4–L5 disc herniation, currently asymptomatic, with physio guidance that excludes heavy spinal loading and loaded spinal flexion. The program will progress gradually, prioritize technique, spine-safe exercise choices, core and hip control, posture and mobility for prolonged sitting, and appropriate recovery/nutrition guidance. I’ll assume clearance from his treating physio/MD to progress with general gym work and that you’ll monitor for any return of symptoms.

High‑level approach
- Goals: increase general strength, improve posture and movement quality, reduce risk of recurrence, improve metabolic health and conditioning.
- Constraints: avoid heavy axial loads through the spine (no heavy back squats, heavy deadlifts, heavy loaded spinal flexion), avoid loaded spinal flexion (no heavy bent‑over loaded rounding movements, loaded sit‑ups/crunches).
- Emphasis: unilateral lower‑body work, hip hinge pattern with safe loading (trap bar deadlift with light–moderate load and technique focus, kettlebell deadlift, Romanian deadlift with light weight and neutral spine), core stability (anti‑flexion, anti‑rotation, anti‑extension), posterior chain and glute strengthening, thoracic mobility, scapular control, conditioning and posture endurance.
- Progression: 3 phases (foundational, strength/hypertrophy, consolidation/transition) across 12 weeks. Frequency: 3 full‑body gym sessions per week (Mon/Wed/Fri or similar) + 1 optional light conditioning/active recovery day. Each gym session ~45–60 min.
- Load guidance: Use RPE 6–8 across phases; avoid sets to absolute failure. Increase load 2.5–5% when last set is comfortably within target RPE. Monitor symptoms — if any low back pain or radicular signs appear, stop and refer to physio/MD.

Structure summary
- Phase 1 (Weeks 1–4): Foundation — movement quality, mobility, light loads, core stability, aerobic base.
- Phase 2 (Weeks 5–8): Strength & capacity — increase load & volume safely, more challenging single‑leg and hinge work, integrated core stability under load.
- Phase 3 (Weeks 9–12): Consolidation & transfer — increase intensity moderately, introduce metabolic and conditioning variations, prepare for long‑term program.

Session template (three sessions per week)
- Warm‑up (10–12 min): breathing & diaphragmatic activation (2–3 min), thoracic mobility and foam rolling (3–4 min), dynamic movement & movement prep specific to session (leg swings, banded glute activation, bodyweight squats or hip hinge practice, scapular pull‑aparts) and 1 light warm‑up set for the main lift.
- Main work (30–40 min): 4–6 exercises per session (1 primary lower, 1 primary upper/pushing, 1 pull, 1 unilateral/lateral, 1 core/anti‑movement, optional conditioning finisher).
- Cool down & mobility (5–8 min): gentle stretching, breathing, posterior chain mobilization, and guidance on sitting breaks.

Detailed week‑by‑week plan

Phase 1 — Foundation (Weeks 1–4)
Goal: re‑establish safe hinge pattern, build core anti‑flexion & anti‑rotation, improve thoracic mobility and glute strength. Moderate volume, light‑moderate loads. Sessions: A, B, C (rotate).

Weeks 1–2
Session A
1) Trap‑bar deadlift (or kettlebell deadlift) — 3 sets x 6–8 reps @ RPE 6–7. Focus neutral spine, hinge from hips. Use moderate load — not maximal.
2) Single‑leg RDL (bodyweight or light dumbbell) — 3 x 8 each leg. Emphasize control and hip hinge.
3) Seated dumbbell shoulder press — 3 x 8–10.
4) TRX row or chest supported row — 3 x 8–10 (chest supported to reduce spinal shear).
5) Pallof press (band) — 3 x 10–12 each side (anti‑rotation).
6) Farmer carry (dumbbells) — 3 x 40–60 m, upright posture.

Session B
1) Goblet squat (light‑moderate) — 3 x 8–10. Keep chest tall, neutral spine.
2) Romanian deadlift with dumbbells (light) — 3 x 8–10.
3) Incline dumbbell press — 3 x 8–10.
4) Lat pull‑down or single‑arm machine row — 3 x 8–10.
5) Side plank — 3 x 20–40 s each side.
6) Glute bridge — 2 x 12–15 (no loaded spine flexion; bar across hips OK if tolerated — keep load moderate).

Session C
1) Step‑ups or Bulgarian split squat — 3 x 8–10 each leg.
2) Kettlebell swing (Russian style, hip hinge, moderate KB) — 3 x 10–12 (light‑moderate; hip drive only, neutral spine).
3) Cable or band face pulls — 3 x 12–15.
4) Chest supported incline T‑row — 3 x 8–10.
5) Bird‑dog (progress to banded variant) — 3 x 8–10 each side.
6) Light conditioning: stationary bike 12–15 min steady or 8 x 30s easy intervals.

Weeks 3–4 — small progressions
- Increase load 5–10% on main lifts if technique good and no symptoms.
- Slightly increase sets where appropriate (e.g., trap‑bar 4 x 6 on Week 4).
- Add intensity to carries (longer distance or heavier but still comfortable).
- Maintain core work; progress Pallof presses by increasing band tension or tempo.

Phase 2 — Strength & capacity (Weeks 5–8)
Goal: increase strength and volume safely, introduce more challenging unilateral work and loaded carries, maintain spine‑safe choices. Progress RPE to 7–8 for main lifts.

Weeks 5–6
Session A
1) Trap‑bar deadlift — 4 x 5 @ RPE 7–8. Emphasize controlled descent, brace, neutral spine.
2) Bulgarian split squat — 3 x 6–8 each leg (add DBs).
3) Seated barbell or dumbbell press — 3 x 6–8.
4) Chest supported row or meadows‑row style supported — 3 x 8.
5) Pallof press — 3 x 8–10 each side (heavier band).
6) Suitcase carry or single‑arm farmer carry — 3 x 40–60 m each side.

Session B
1) Split Romanian deadlift (dumbbells) — 4 x 6 each leg.
2) Goblet or safety‑bar front squat (safety bar reduces spinal load) — 3 x 6–8. If safety bar not available, keep goblet moderate.
3) Pull‑up or assisted pull‑up — 3 x 6–8.
4) Cable horizontal row (seated) — 3 x 8–10.
5) Plank with marching progression — 3 x 30–45 s.
6) Conditioning: moderate bike or row 12–15 min steady.

Session C
1) Hex/trap bar deadlift deficit or variation (only if clean form) — 3 x 5 (moderate).
2) Step‑ups with weight — 3 x 8 each leg.
3) Incline dumbbell press — 3 x 6–8.
4) Face pulls + external rotation superset — 3 x 12.
5) Anti‑extension holds: front plank progression (weighted only if neutral spine guaranteed) — 3 x 30–60 s.
6) Kettlebell swing moderate — 3 x 12–15.

Weeks 7–8 — increase intensity and complexity
- Increase trap‑bar/deadlifts set weight modestly (aim for 1–2 reps increase or 5% load).
- Add a heavy-ish farmer carry or suitcase carry set (heavier but controlled).
- Introduce tempo on some reps (e.g., slow 3s eccentric on goblet/front squat).
- Progress core: Pallof with longer holds, plank with alternating limb lifts.

Phase 3 — Consolidation & transfer (Weeks 9–12)
Goal: solidify strength gains, increase metabolic conditioning, prepare for maintenance/next phase. Maintain spine safety; optional higher intensity conditioning.

Weeks 9–10
Session A
1) Trap‑bar deadlift — 4 x 4 @ RPE 7.5–8 (moderate to slightly heavier).
2) Reverse lunge (dumbbell) — 3 x 6–8 each leg.
3) Seated overhead press (DB) — 4 x 6–8.
4) Single‑arm chest supported row or one‑arm cable row — 3 x 8.
5) Pallof press or anti‑rotation cable hold — 3 x 10 each side.
6) Farmer carry heavy-ish — 3 x 45–60 m.

Session B
1) Safety‑bar or front squat — 4 x 5 (front loading keeps spine more upright).
2) Romanian deadlift (moderate) — 3 x 6–8.
3) Pull‑up / weighted if possible — 4 x 5–6.
4) Face pulls + band pull‑aparts — 3 x 12.
5) Hollow body prone holds submax (avoid flexion repetitions) or dead bug progression — 3 x 30–40 s.
6) Conditioning: interval row/bike 10 x 30s moderate with 60s easy.

Session C
1) Single‑leg deadlift with KB — 3 x 8 each.
2) Step‑ups or Bulgarian split with pause — 3 x 6–8 each.
3) Incline DB press — 3 x 6–8.
4) Seated cable row — 3 x 8–10.
5) Anti‑extension rollout alternative: standing cable anti‑extension (kneeling rollouts avoided if provokes flexion) — 3 x 8–10.
6) Kettlebell swings complex: 4 x 12 moderate.

Weeks 11–12 — consolidation, slight taper for assessment
- Week 11: maintain intensity, possibly add a small 1–2 rep increase in main lifts if tolerated.
- Week 12: reduce volume by ~20–30% (deload style) to consolidate adaptations and reduce fatigue.

Session examples for Week 12 (lower volume)
A
- Trap‑bar deadlift 3 x 4 moderate
- Bulgarian split squat 2 x 6 each
- Seated DB press 3 x 6
- Chest supported row 3 x 8
- Pallof 2 x 8 each
- Farmer carry 2 x 40m

B
- Front/safety‑bar squat 3 x 4–5
- RDL 3 x 6
- Pull‑up 3 x 5
- Face pulls 3 x 12
- Dead bug 3 x 12
- Easy 10 min bike cooldown

Monitoring and technique notes
- Always cue neutral spine, hip hinge (push hips back), bracing (diaphragmatic breathing), and avoid breath‑holding Valsalva on near‑max loads.
- Replace any exercise that provokes back pain with lower‑impact alternative (e.g., replace trap‑bar deadlift with kettlebell deadlift or hip thrust if symptoms appear).
- Use chest‑supported/bench‑supported rows and presses where possible to reduce shear on the spine.
- Avoid loaded spinal flexion exercises (no heavy bent‑over rows with unsupported torso, no weighted sit‑ups, no heavy rounded back lifting).
- Gradual progression: 2–5% load increases/week when patient comfortable.
- Encourage 1–2 sessions/week of walking or low‑impact cardio (20–40 min) for circulation and recovery.

Core and posture work (ongoing)
- Daily micro‑sessions (5 min) for desk posture: diaphragmatic breathing, thoracic extension mobilizations, band pull‑aparts, scapular squeezes, glute bridges (bodyweight), and hip flexor soft tissue work.
- Break up sitting every 30–45 minutes: stand, walk, or perform mobility breaks for 2–3 minutes.

Rehab‑specific considerations
- If physiotherapist prescribed specific exercises, integrate them into warm‑up or accessory slots (e.g., specific activation drills, neural mobilizations).
- If any recurrence of radiculopathy, numbness/tingling, or acute back pain occurs, stop loading immediately and refer back to physio/MD.

Nutrition & recovery guidance (brief)
- Protein: aim for ~1.2–1.6 g/kg body weight/day to support strength and recovery (adjust to client goals).
- Calories: mild calorie surplus if aiming to gain strength/size; maintenance for strength focus; deficit not recommended while building technical base unless needed for weight loss with conservative intensity.
- Hydration and sleep: target 7–9 hours sleep/night; hydrate across day.
- Anti‑inflammatory diet focus: whole foods, include omega‑3 sources, limit processed foods and high refined sugars that can impede recovery.
- Recovery: active recovery days (walking, mobility), foam rolling, targeted soft tissue work for hips/glutes/hamstrings/ITB as needed.

Progress tracking and reassessment
- Reassess movement quality and symptom status every 2–4 weeks. Track performance (loads, RPE), pain scores (0–10), and functional measures (single‑leg balance, timed carries).
- After 12 weeks, consider testing 3–5 rep maxes on trap‑bar deadlift and front squat with conservative approach, or transition into an intermediate program tailored to goals.

Sample week schedule (Week 6 example)
- Monday (Session A): trap‑bar 4x5, Bulgarian split 3x6, seated DB press 3x6, chest‑supported row 3x8, Pallof 3x8, suitcase carry 3x40m.
- Tuesday: 20–30 min walk + 5 min desk mobility
- Wednesday (Session B): split RDL 4x6, goblet/front squat 3x6–8, pull‑up 3x6, cable row 3x8, plank march 3x30s, 12 min steady bike.
- Thursday: mobility and soft tissue
- Friday (Session C): trap‑bar variant 3x5, step‑ups 3x8, incline DB press 3x6–8, face pulls 3x12, dead bug 3x10, KB swings 3x12.
- Weekend: 1 easy active recovery session (walk/cycling) + mobility

If you want, I can:
- Provide printable session cards for each week (exercise, sets, reps, tempo, cues).
- Adjust the plan for specific equipment availability (e.g., no trap bar) or specific client goals (fat loss, hypertrophy, maximal strength).
- Add sample nutrition days or a calorie/protein calculator based on his bodyweight.

Would you like printable weekly PDFs or a version adapted for limited equipment? Also tell me his bodyweight if you want tailored nutrition numbers.
